sources.sub: {project}. What Canonico reads, how mail reaches it, and how emails are routed.
sources.emptyText: Connect documents, a document library, a public GitHub repository, a mailbox or an inbound webhook. Canonico extracts facts and keeps their versions.
sources.comingSoon: Real mail, SharePoint and Google Drive connectors are coming soon. This demo uses sample data.

mail.title: Mail settings
mail.ownConfig: This project uses its own mail configuration.
mail.inheritedFrom: Set on {org} and inherited by every project unless overridden.
mail.reverted: This project now uses the organisation mail settings
mail.overrideDone: This project now has its own mail settings
mail.overrideSub: Give this project its own inbound address. Everything else stays as set on the organisation.

rules.title: Routing rules
rules.empty: No routing rules. Emails stay in the organisation inbox.
rules.dialogSub: Emails from this sender domain are routed to the project. First match wins, lowest priority first.
rules.priorityErr: Priority must be a whole number.
rules.testHelp: Checks the rules in order without sending anything.
rules.testNone: No rule matches. The email stays in the organisation inbox and creates no facts.

messages.title: Last emails routed here
messages.emptyText: Emails from senders that match a rule for this project arrive here. Send the demo email from Demo control to try it.

settings.sub: {org} · organisation, webhooks, tag rules, members and roles.

members.footer: A project role overrides the organisation role for that project only.
members.inviteSub: They join {org} with the role you pick. Project roles can override it later.
members.name: Name

hook.title: Organisation webhook
hook.intro: One URL for the whole organisation. Each item is routed to a project by its tags, using the tag rules.
hook.shownOnce: Copy it now. It is shown once, then only {last4}.
hook.rotateHelp: Sent as the X-Canonico-Token header. Rotating stops the old secret at once.
hook.rotated: Secret rotated. Copy the new one now.

tagrules.title: Tag rules
tagrules.sub: first match wins · lowest priority first
tagrules.empty: No tag rules. Items posted to the organisation webhook stay in the inbox.
tagrules.dialogSub: Items with this tag are routed to the project. First match wins, lowest priority first.
tagrules.priorityErr: Priority must be a whole number.
tagrules.testHelp: Checks the rules in order without creating anything. topic: tags force the topic.
tagrules.testNone: No rule matches. The item stays in the organisation inbox and creates no facts.

setup.railSub: Four short steps. Every value can be changed later in Settings.
setup.d1: The organisation is the global brain. Projects inside it stay isolated from each other.
setup.domainHelp: Used to invite members and for the default mail routing rule.
setup.d2: Set once for the organisation. Every project inherits it unless it overrides it.
setup.imapSub: Mocked in this demo, polled every minute
setup.inboundHelp: Forward or BCC emails here. Routing rules decide the project.
setup.d3: A project holds its own sources and facts. Nothing leaks between projects.
setup.projRule: Route emails from {domain} to this project
setup.projRuleSub: Creates a routing rule you can change later in Sources.
setup.d4: Canonico reads the sample corpus first. You can add more sources at any time from Sources.
setup.d4done: Canonico read every source and extracted facts.
setup.corpusSub: OIDA ClearPath documents, emails and notes
setup.errDomain: Enter a domain like company.com, without @.
setup.alreadyDone: This organisation is already set up.
setup.ready: {org} is set up. Ask your first question.
